uniequip_002_vigil:
The shoe-shiner trembles as he enters the Bellone famiglia parlor.
He trembles not because this is Bellone territory. He had shined Bernardo's shoes for thirty years, and the man always respected those who respected him. The last time he had stepped into this parlor, it was so that he could offer Bernardo the chance to name his son.
His fear comes from the fact that the one sitting here today is not Bernardo, but his son, Leontuzzo.
He has not heard much about the Bellone heir. All he knew was that the young master had never come to him for a shoe shining.
'My father isn't here at the moment, but you can trust me as you trusted him.'
His words calm him a bit, allowing the shoe-shiner to explain why he had no choice but to come:
His son leads a decent, honorable life, and fell in love with a lady from Columbia. However, that lady was also being pursued by a maniac who didn't take kindly to a rival. Three nights ago, his son was cornered by that maniac and beaten within an inch of his life. He'd sought aid from the courts, but the man belonged to a Columbian famiglia, and his lawyers were easily able to secure a 'not guilty.'
'When I was leaving the courtroom, he stepped in front of me and shoved two banknotes into my pocket. He laughed as he told me it was for my son's medical fees. I...' The shoe-shiner went on, tears streaming from his wizened eyes.
Leontuzzo listens in silence. He knows that if his father were here, he would surely give the old man a pat on the shoulder, acknowledge his suffering, then provide a solution to this. A humane way.
Generally speaking, these things could only be resolved with bloodshed.
But that was not how he does things.
'What is it you wish for, signor?'
'I have no requests, Don Leontuzzo, other than justice for my boy.'
'Justice. Am I to understand that you want this man to feel the same pain your son did?'
'That's right. Nothing more.'
Leontuzzo snaps his fingers, and a red-headed young man steps out from a door to the side.
'Demetri, go investigate the gang behind that guy first.'
'Easy enough, but what comes next?'
'Next... If I'm not mistaken, those Columbian gangs want to sidestep us and cozy up to the local government. Then let's propose sending local 'talents' to the Columbian frontier. Hopefully, every famiglia will enthusiastically agree. Let them send off a few stronzi who should have been exiled long ago.'
The red-headed youth snaps his fingers. 'So we'll ship this guy off too?'
'Exactly.'
'Capisco.'
With that final declaration, the man leaves the room. Leontuzzo turns towards the astonished shoe-shiner. 'This is the justice I can give you. Are you satisfied with it, signor?'
The shoe-shiner quickly catches on, and his gaze turns from astonishment to gratitude.
'Take this.'
'This is...'
'My pistola. Place it by your shoe-shiner, and nobody will cause you trouble.'
'But—'
'Don't worry. I barely use it. Whenever you feel like you can sleep easy again, just give it back to the guard downstairs.'
uniequip_003_vigil:
Leontuzzo is somewhat nervous in the driver's seat. Today is the first time he's officially driving a car.
Look both ways. Adjust the seat. Adjust the rear-view mirror. Fasten the seatbelt. Check the gear. Once all these steps are complete, he looks at the passenger seat with some trepidation. Lavinia sits there, his instructor for the day. Only once she nods does he let out a faint sigh of relief, turn the key, and start the engine. The car slowly trundles out the garage and onto the street.
The streets are, as always, showered in a patter of drizzle. Leontuzzo flicks the windshield wipers, taking care to keep his foot on the brake, and not daring to go too fast.
'You're driving far too slowly, Leon. You'll never learn anything like that.' Her role as driving instructor has not given her cause to loosen her usual strictness.
'The more you remind me, the more nervous I get, Lavinia.' Leontuzzo has a death grip on the steering wheel, his eyes locked onto the road ahead, refusing to turn his head even an inch.
'Who was it at breakfast who was <i>so excited to show off his skills to Demetri once he got back?'
'I let the steam from the bread get to my head.'
As they speak, the car reaches an intersection. Just as the red lights are about to go green, several pedestrians cross. However, the moment they see the emblem atop the oncoming car, they immediately lower their heads and hurry down the rest of the crosswalk.
Unfortunately for one of them, they trip and fall as they do so.
Lavinia looks at Leontuzzo, as if asking him: 'What should you do in this situation?'
'...I should slam the accelerator and run the red light. Best to give them a splash and a little scare.'
But even as he says this, he presses down on the brake, letting the car slowly come to a stop in front of the crosswalk.
The fallen pedestrian clambers back to their feet, giving the two in the car a slight nod of thanks before quickly leaving the scene.
'If most famiglia members drove like you, I'd be able to shave off a tenth of the cases I preside over each year, if only for minor incidents like just now.' Lavinia speaks with approval of his action.
'Honestly, there are simply too many traffic laws. I'm not keen on remembering them all either.' The light turns green, and Leontuzzo restarts the car. 'But there's one thing I've come to realize lately. We follow these so-called laws not because they are natural to us, but because they are self-evident principles we as a people discover as we seek justice.'
'Well said, Leon. It seems you have a thorough understanding of those traffic laws after all. Now let's see if you can actually remember them.'
'Oddio, Lavinia, are you seriously going to give a lecture <i>here?'
'I <i>did promise your father to teach you everything I know. So, Leon, what are those white lines by the side of the car meant to indicate?'
'Wait, give me some time to think...'
The rains of Siracusa are endless and suffocating, but at the very least, inside this car, the warmth of chatter can be felt.
